item.text: {"text":"Time-dependent recurrent gates have direct precedent: [MTAM (CIKM 2020)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08598) incorporates temporal information into GRU state transitions and attention to connect short-term intent with historical memory. More recently, [TSRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08531) models user-specific repeat intervals, item-specific intervals, and similarity between repeat sequences. These support investigating context-dependent retention, but provide no evidence of gains on this pinned Amazon benchmark. Repeat-item mechanisms also have limited applicability when recommendations exclude previously consumed items; recurring interests may still help rank unseen related items.\n\nText-based recent results require careful filtering. [CALRec (RecSys 2024)](https://research.google/pubs/calrec-contrastive-alignment-of-generative-llms-for-sequential-recommendation/) aligns textual item representations and sequential behavior using pretrained PaLM-2, so its implementation violates the no-pretrained-model constraint. A compatible experimental hypothesis is a small, randomly initialized token embedding table with pooled title/description features, jointly trained with item IDs and the GRU. Condition retention on observed log time gaps, current item features, and previous hidden state; mask padding updates and read the final nonpadding position. Keep all components inside one jointly trained model per category. Compare gates first, then text features, using macro validation HR@10; neither improvement nor simulator compatibility should be assumed."}
